title: Causal descent on intergenerational housing × companionship
objective: Discriminate the governing causes of the retained institution-based intergenerational housing/companionship exchange before any missing-edge or business claim.
truth_rules: A GOVERNANCE FUNCTION CAN BE REAL WITHOUT BEING AN OPEN MISSING EDGE

evidence.fact: A long-running Suzhou participant reported that a comparable room would normally cost around RMB 2,000/month while her eldercare-institution room cost RMB 200/month; rent pressure was an explicit reason for joining.
The same Suzhou program initially received roughly 40–50 applicants and selected five, while the highlighted participant had remained for more than two years.
Shanghai's 2026 policy response explicitly identifies youth rent cost and commute pressure as part of the intergenerational-co-living problem statement.
The Suzhou participant also described loneliness after arriving in the city and a family-like sense of warmth inside the institution.

youth_secondary.limit: Secondary relational value is plausible but current evidence does not show that it independently creates the exchange without the housing-price wedge.

evidence.fact: Shanghai's 2026 response frames the model as a way to enrich older residents' spiritual/social life through bounded non-professional companionship.
Changzhou's operating program explicitly routes youth contribution into teaching, reading companionship and activity support rather than professional care replacement.

older_adult.limit: The social outcome is repeatedly stated and observed qualitatively, but payer willingness and quantified incremental outcome remain unproven.

evidence.fact: Shanghai reports citywide eldercare bed utilization at 62% in 2025 and continues policy work to improve utilization and address persistent empty-capacity mismatches.
Shanghai's August 2026 response makes annual bed utilization, occupancy stability and empty-capacity remediation core operating metrics tied to support policy.

institution.limit: Citywide empty bed capacity does not prove that those beds/rooms are legally or operationally suitable for youth residence. Some programs use employee dormitory or separately designated rooms.

causal_hypothesis_verdicts.reason: Large price wedges, explicit rent-pressure narratives and applicant surplus show that low-cost housing is a real youth-side pump.
causal_hypothesis_verdicts.not_sufficient_because: It does not explain why eldercare institutions should supply rooms or absorb governance burden.

causal_hypothesis_verdicts.reason: Institutional occupancy imbalance is real and policy-visible, but youth accommodation may use separate rooms/dormitories rather than otherwise saleable eldercare beds.
causal_hypothesis_verdicts.not_sufficient_because: A low citywide utilization rate is not equivalent to a dense pool of legally convertible youth rooms.

causal_hypothesis_verdicts.reason: Multiple programs explicitly target companionship, emotional support and younger social presence.
causal_hypothesis_verdicts.not_sufficient_because: Current evidence does not isolate the incremental outcome or establish a private payer for it.

evidence.fact: Beijing's institution-based trial requires applicant screening, medical/psychological checks, signed agreements, training, monthly service thresholds, satisfaction thresholds and explicit exit conditions.
Jinyun research records background checks, staff coordination, schedule conflict, lifestyle conflict, language barriers and retention/participation difficulty.
National 2026 eldercare safety rules strengthen whole-process safety responsibility and accountability for eldercare institutions.

causal_hypothesis_verdicts.inference: The institution already bears custody/safety/operational responsibility and therefore naturally performs local screening, rule-setting, monitoring and exit. The governance function is real, but current evidence does not show it as an unowned inter-node edge available to an independent Rooter.

causal_hypothesis_verdicts.reason: Current China cases are commonly government-guided and institution-operated, use volunteer framing and heavily discounted accommodation, while the institution absorbs ongoing coordination and risk.

evidence.fact: Shanghai's planned model is explicitly government-guided, institution-led and socially participated; it is also considering a municipal digital platform.
Beijing recruitment is routed through a public volunteer platform while each eldercare institution performs final selection, training, contracting and supervision.

structural_model.implication: The institution is not merely a supply node. It is part of the exchange mechanism and is the natural local control-plane owner.

evidence.fact: Homeshare UK reports average recurring fees paid by both householders and homesharers to cover matching/support, with no rent paid between the two parties.
Homeshare International says most surveyed programs were charities/not-for-profits, only a few were businesses, and some charge fees to cover administration.
UK good-practice guidance describes fees funding screening, checks, matching, ongoing monitoring and support.

international_adjacent_mechanism.interpretation: Professional governance/matching is a real economic function. However, mature analogues often look like cost-recovery social infrastructure rather than proof of high-margin control-plane economics.

china_evidence.fact: A 2026 People's Daily-family report discusses 'shared children' and recommends exploring low-cost rooms from older adults with idle housing in exchange for nearby companionship/help.
china_evidence.evidence_role: policy/commentary suggestion, not an executed domestic household-homeshare flow

private_household_variant.search_result: No strong current executed mainland-China household-homeshare program was established in this scan. Existing domestic evidence remains institution-centered.
private_household_variant.international_counterexample: Household homeshare is operational and fee-supported in other countries, so the mechanism is possible, but geographic transfer cannot be promoted without local leakage.

accepted: Youth demand is primarily powered by an unusually large affordable-housing price wedge.
Older-adult value is primarily ordinary social contact/companionship, not professional care substitution.
Institution value plausibly combines suitable-space utilization, social-service outcomes and policy/brand value.
The exchange requires high-touch local governance because vulnerable residents, residence and volunteer obligations coexist.
causal_frontier.stopping_reason: The deepest intervention-relevant constraint identified is governed co-residence, but in current China institution-based cases that constraint is already owned by the institution/public program that bears safety and operating responsibility. No independent recurring missing edge is established.

preserve_as: EVIDENCE THAT HOUSING PRICE WEDGES CAN MOBILIZE YOUTH INTO SOCIAL-CONTRIBUTION FLOWS
EVIDENCE THAT GOVERNED CO-RESIDENCE REQUIRES SCREENING/RULES/MONITORING/EXIT
primary_decision.commercial_reason: The natural local control plane is currently the eldercare institution/public program itself. A separate Rooter layer would need direct evidence that institutions repeatedly fail at a portable governance function they are willing to pay an external operator to own; that evidence is absent.

next_action: Return to broad fresh life-world sensing. Keep private-household homeshare only as a watchlist/geographic-transfer hypothesis and reactivate it only if current mainland-China executed leakage appears. Do not build an institution co-living platform, screening product or outsourced program without direct buyer-side failure evidence.
